summary: Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Min Thu Wun (1909–2004) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1926–1935) under Pe Maung Tin (~1927–1935) and at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Minakshi Banerjee is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar. She held the James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Ming Chen works in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He has held appointments at Peking University, including as a professor (attested 2001, 2013).

Ming Mei works in Buddhist studies. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and also studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He earned a BA at the University of Hong Kong and a PhD at UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en, later serving as professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Mingqian Xu specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2010–2013), worked there as a project research assistant (2013–2015), and completed a PhD at National Chengchi University (2016–2023).
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Mini Verma specializes in Indology and other fields. She held posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (2006–2007), Sai Group of Institutions (2007–2013), IMS Noida (2013), and Jagannath Institute of Management Sciences, Noida (2022).

Minori Nishimura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Taisho University. He held positions at Taisho University, the Sanko Cultural Institute, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Minoru Hara (1930–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He taught at the University of Tokyo and served as president of ICPBS and director of the IIBS.

Minoru Inaba works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Kyoto University, he worked at Tokuyama Corporation, as assistant professor at Kyoto University, and as professor at Doshisha University.

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo before serving as a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from circa 1963 to 1994.

Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Strasbourg. He was Associate Professor of Latin at Johns Hopkins, directed the American School of Classical Studies in Rome, and became professor at Harvard.
Minyak Kunzang Sonam studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Mio Kishimoto is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1979) and held academic posts at Ochanomizu University (~1979–1994) and as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi and Robert A. F. Thurman, and completed postdoctoral work under Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Bucharest and Calcutta, and held posts at Bucharest, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, the Sorbonne, and the University of Chicago.
